title: Κηπουρὸς ⟨ἀρδεύων λάχανα⟩
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 154. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κηπουρῷ τις ἐπιστὰς ἀρδεύοντι τὰ λάχανα ἐπυνθάνετο αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν δι’ ἣν τὰ μὲν ἄγρια τῶν λαχάνων εὐθαλῆ τέ ἐστι καὶ στερεά, τὰ δὲ ἥμερα λεπτὰ καὶ μεμαρασμένα.
sentences.tr: Kēpourōi tis epistas ardeuonti ta lachana epynthaneto autou tēn aitian di’ hēn ta men agria tōn lachanōn euthalē te esti kai sterea, ta de hēmera lepta kai memarasmena.
sentences.l: A certain man, having stood over a gardener watering his vegetables, inquired of him the reason on account of which the wild sort of vegetables are both flourishing and firm, while the cultivated ones are thin and shrivelled.
sentences.i: A man came and stood over a gardener as he was watering his vegetables, and asked him why the wild plants are lush and sturdy, while the ones under cultivation are thin and shrivelled.
sentences.n: ἐπιστάς, "having stood over", is the regular way of saying that one person comes up to another at his work. πυνθάνομαι takes the genitive of the person questioned (αὐτοῦ) and the accusative of the thing asked. Of plants, ἥμερος is "tame, under cultivation", the standing opposite of ἄγριος, "wild". μεμαρασμένα is the perfect passive participle of μαραίνω, "waste away": not withering now, but withered and staying so. The title's ⟨ ⟩ mark words Chambry supplies.

sentences.t: Κἀκεῖνος ἔφη· « Ἡ γῆ τῶν μὲν μήτηρ ἐστί, τῶν δὲ μητρυιά. »
sentences.tr: Kakeinos ephē· « Hē gē tōn men mētēr esti, tōn de mētruia. »
sentences.l: And he said: « The earth is mother of the one sort, and stepmother of the other. »
sentences.n: Κἀκεῖνος is καὶ ἐκεῖνος run together by crasis, and Chambry prints the coronis over the α. The genitives τῶν μέν … τῶν δέ pick up the two kinds of plant from the question. A μητρυιά in Greek life is proverbially the grudging carer, and the word carries that charge without further comment.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν παίδων οὐχ ὁμοίως τρέφονται οἱ ὑπὸ μητρυιᾶς τρεφόμενοι τοῖς μητέρας ἔχουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn paidōn ouch homoiōs trephontai hoi hypo mētruias trephomenoi tois mēteras echousin.
sentences.l: So too, among children, those who are reared by a stepmother are not reared in the same way as those who have mothers.
sentences.n: ὁμοίως takes the dative of the party compared with — τοῖς … ἔχουσιν, "as those who have mothers". Article plus participle is Greek's ordinary way of saying "those who…", twice over here.
